analysis:
The two units are BASE text of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (base lines 583-1257). The file changes are documentation-only: a new optional Swift-only `detail` field on model_autopilot_status (head ~854), new Autopilot-download prefetch_model_status error codes (head 877-896), and further edits later in the file that are not supplied in these units. I saw only a truncated patch excerpt, so I could not examine the head-side lines past ~896. No source code changes are in this batch.

Security-relevant observations on the visible text:
- The `detail` field is an optional, diagnostic-only field. The base doc already states that status text is "not an authorization or capacity signal", so it creates no new trust grant. The excerpt says it is sent "with consent", which limits disclosure of busy reasons to the coordinator, and older coordinators ignore it.
- The new prefetch error codes are closed vocabulary (model_not_selected, autopilot_paused, model_not_supported, model_limit_reached), which limits free-form leakage. They also suggest provider-side policy checks on Autopilot downloads, such as consent, a catalog manifest and a 256-ID bound.
- The base text for model_autopilot and model_autopilot_control keeps the existing controls: session and revision binding, an expiry window, an explicit selected-model allowlist, shadow leases granting no authority, and immutable command-ID payload checks.

Open integration questions for the next pass: (1) whether the rest of the truncated patch, including the Autopilot state, busy reasons and any new coordinator-driven download or prefetch command, weakens the selected-model allowlist or consent boundary (TB-002, A-004, T-012); (2) whether the busy-reason `detail` string can carry sensitive local state (process or app names) to the coordinator. This cannot be determined from the supplied evidence. No concrete regression is established here, so there are no findings.
